summary.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa.” It is analyzed as a compound in which 父 supplies the father meaning and 巴 is proposed as a sound component.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 父 contributes meaning and 巴 is proposed as a sound cue. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, 巴 is reconstructed as *praː and 爸 as *praːs. This comparison supports the proposed sound role, though 巴’s original name and referent are unsettled.

components.text: 父 contributes the meaning “father.” A transmitted Shuowen account describes 父 as a family head holding a staff, but does not establish that description as the component’s original pictorial meaning in 爸. The selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 父 alone, not an early form of 爸.

巴 is proposed as the sound component. A selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 巴 alone, not an attestation of 爸. The Shuowen tradition links 巴 to a giant snake, while another proposal interprets early forms as a kneeling person; neither referent is established.

sound.text: The proposed sound comparison is 巴 *praː and 爸 *praːs in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system. 巴’s original name is not established, so its depicted referent cannot independently confirm this comparison.

history.text: 爸 is reported absent from Shuowen. Guangya groups 爸 with 爹 and 㸙 under the gloss “father,” a record of the word’s use rather than a date for the graph’s formation. The selected oracle-style illustrations show 父 and 巴 separately; they do not establish an earlier 爸 form or a sequence of graphic change.

A historical dictionary transmits an account in which 父 was added to a father word written 八八 or 巴巴. A later study instead argues that the father word is phonologically from 父. These are competing explanations; the formation sequence of the graph is not established.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic analysis is reported, but no early inscription or dated sequence of the complete graph shows when 父 and 巴 were combined.

巴’s early form is disputed: the Shuowen tradition associates it with a giant snake, while another proposal interprets forms read as 巴 as a kneeling person. Neither account establishes its original referent or name, limiting independent confirmation of its proposed sound role in 爸.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source for the father word and the claim that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父 are not independently substantiated here. These lexical claims are separate from the proposed 巴 sound component.

senses.period: Three Kingdoms era (reported dating of the Guangya record)
senses.text: A Guangya entry is reported to gloss 爸 as “father.” This records the word’s use; it does not establish a dated physical witness for the graph.
Modern references gloss 爸 as “father” and “papa”; no separate historical stage for “papa” is established.

limitations.text: The recorded “father” gloss does not date the graph’s formation, and the evidence does not establish a chronological development from “father” to “papa.”

overview.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa”: 父 supplies the meaning, while 巴 is proposed as a sound cue. The proposed sound link is uncertain because 巴’s original name is unsettled.

components.text: 父 contributes the father meaning. Its selected oracle-style image is a redraw of 父 alone, not an early 爸.
巴 is proposed as the sound component, though its original referent and name remain unsettled.

relationships.text: 父 contributes the father meaning in the reported phonosemantic analysis of 爸.
巴 is proposed as a sound component, compared with 爸 as *praː and *praːs respectively in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system. 巴’s original name is unsettled.
